name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | Data Structures | Test 2

question.text:
Consider Iterated logarithm of $n$, written log ${ }^{\star} n$. Defined as below.
$$\lg ^{*} N=\min \{k \mid \underbrace{\lg \lg \cdots \lg }_{k} N \leq 1\}$$
Which of the following is TRUE?

(log base can be considered as any constant)

  1. $\lg \lg { }^{*} n=o\left(\lg ^{*} \lg n\right)$ here o is small oh
  2. $\lg ^{*} \lg n=o\left(\lg \lg ^{*} n\right)$ here $o$ is small oh
  3. $\lg ^{*} \lg n=\boldsymbol{\Theta}\left(\lg \lg { }^{*} n\right)$
  4. $\lg ^{\star} \lg n$ and $\lg \lg ^{\ast} n$ are not comparable

Let $\text{S}_{1}= \displaystyle{}\sum_{r=0}^{\log n-1} \frac{n r}{2^{r}}$, and $\text{S}_{2} = \displaystyle{} \sum_{r=0}^{\log n-1} r 2^{r}$.
Which of the following is true?

  1. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n \log n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n \log n)$
  2. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n \log n)$
  3. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n \log n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n)$
  4. $\text{S}_{1}=\Theta(n), \text{S}_{2}=\Theta(n)$

Which of the following statement is FALSE?

  1. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $(f(n))^{2}= \Theta\left((g(n))^{2}\right)$
  2. If $f(n)=\mathcal{O}(g(n))$ and $f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$, then we have $f(n)=g(n)$
  3. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(3^{n}\right)$
  4. $2^{n}+n^{2}=\mathcal{O}\left(2^{n}\right)$

What is the time complexity of code given?

int fun(int n)
{
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = n; i > 0; i /= 2)
    for (int j = 0; j < i; j++)
        count += 1;
    return count;
}
  1. $\Theta(\log n)$
  2. $\Theta(n)$
  3. $\Theta(n \log n)$
  4. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$

Consider $\text{Iterated logarithm}$ of $n,$ written $\log^\ast n$ (usually read "$\log$ star $n$"), is the number of times the logarithm (base $2$) function must be iteratively applied before the result is less than or equal to $1.$
Mathematically,
$$\lg ^{*} N=\min \{k \mid \underbrace{\lg \lg \cdots \lg }_{k} N \leq 1\}$$
For example-
$\begin{aligned} \lg ^{*} 2 &=1,\\
\lg ^{*} 4 &=2,\\
\lg ^{*} 16 &=3,\\
\lg ^{*} 65536 &=4,\\
\lg ^{*}\left(2^{65536}\right) &=5 \end{aligned}$

Which of the following is/are correct about the implementation of $\log ^{*} n?$

In all options, $\log()$ is a function which calculates $\log$ base $2$ of a given number.

  1.  
    int iteratedLog(double n)
{
    if (n > 1.0) {
        return 1 + iteratedLog( log(n));
    }
    else return 0;
}
  2.  
    int iteratedLog(double n)
{
    int count=0;
    while (n > 1.0) {
        n = log(n);
        count++;
    }
    return count;
}
  3. $\log ^* n=\left\{\begin{array}{clc}0 & \text { if } & n \leq 1\\
    1+\log^*(\log n) & \text { if } & n>1\end{array}\right.$

     
  4. $\log ^*\left(2^m\right)= \begin{cases}1+\log ^*(m) & \text { if } m>1 \\ 0 & \text { if } m \leq 0 \\ 1 & \text { if } 0<m \leq 1\end{cases}$

Consider the function $f(N)=\displaystyle{}\sum_{i=0}^{N} \sum_{j=0}^{i} j$

Which of the following is true about $f(N)?$

  1. $f(N)=\Theta\left(N^{2}\right)$
  2. $f(N)=\Theta\left(N^{3}\right)$
  3. $f(N)=\Theta(N)$
  4. $f(N)=\Theta(N \log N)$

fun(int N) {
    for (int i = N; i > 0; i = i / 2) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i * 2; j += 1) {
            printf("Hello World");
        }
    }
}
  1. $\Theta(N \log N)$
  2. $\Theta(N)$
  3. $\Theta(\log N)$
  4. $\Theta\left((\log N)^{2}\right)$

Consider two statements $\mathrm{S} 1$ and $\mathrm{S} 2$ below.

  • $\mathrm{S} 1:$ An $\Theta(n \log n)$ algorithm ALWAYS runs faster than an $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$ algorithm.
  • $\mathrm{S} 2:$ An $\Theta(n \log n)$ algorithm ALWAYS runs slower than an $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$ algorithm.

Which of the following is correct ?

  1. $\mathrm{S} 1$ is true but $\mathrm{S} 2$ is false
  2. $\mathrm{S} 1$ is false but $\mathrm{S} 2$ is true
  3. Both statements are true
  4. Both Statements are false

Assume you have two positive functions $f$ and $g$ such that $f(n)$ is in $O(g(n))$. For each of the following statements, decide which one(s) is/are always TRUE.

  1. $2^{f(n)}$ is $O\left(2^{g(n)}\right)$
  2. $f(n)^{2}$ is $O\left(g(n)^{2}\right)$
  3. $f(n)=O\left((f(n))^{2}\right)$
  4. $g(n)=\Omega(g(n))$

Which of the following(s) is/are TRUE?

  1. $ \displaystyle{}\sum_{i=0}^{n} 5^{-i}=\Theta(n)$
     
  2. $2^{\log _{4} n}=\Theta(\sqrt{n})$
     
  3. $\displaystyle{}\sum_{i=1}^{\log m} c 2^{2 i}=O\left(4^{\log m}\right)$
     
  4. $\displaystyle{}\sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{n^{2}}{\mathrm{i} \log \mathrm{n}}=\Omega\left(\mathrm{n}^{3}\right)$

If $g(n)= \Omega(n)$ and $h(n)=O(n)$ then $g(n) . h(n)$ will be -

  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $O(n)$
  3. $\Omega(n)$
  4. None of these

Suppose we perform a sequence of $n$ operations on a data structure in which the $i$ th operation costs $i$ if $i$ is an exact power of $2,$ and $1$ otherwise.
Let $C_{i}$ be cost of $i$ th operation then -
$$ C_{i}= \begin{cases}i & \text { if } \mathrm{i} \text { is an exact power of } 2\\
1 & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}$$
What will be the total cost of $n$ operations?

  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(n \log n)$
  3. $\Theta\left(2^{n}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left(n 2^{n}\right)$

Which of the following statement is/are FALSE? Assume that $\log$ base is $2$ in all options.

  1. $8^{\log \left(n^{2}\right)} \in \Theta\left(n^{6}\right)$
  2. If $f, g$, and $h$ are functions from the natural numbers to the non-negative real numbers with $f(n) \geq g(n) \forall n \geq 1, f(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$, and $g(n) \in \Theta(h(n))$, then $(f(n)-g(n)) \in \Theta(h(n))$
  3. $(\log n)^{a}$ is $\mathrm{O}\left(n^{ b}\right)$ for any constant $a$, and for any constant $b>0$
  4. $T(n) = O(f(n))$ and $g(n)$ is a function whose value is never negative then $g(n) T(n)$ is $O(g(n) f(n))$

Arrange the following functions in their increasing order of growth. In options $\log ^{2} n$ means $(\log n)^{2}$

  1. $\log (n !),  \log ^{2} n, (\lg n) !,  e^{n}$
  2. $\log (n !),  \log ^{2} n,  e^{n}, (\lg n) !$
  3. $\log ^{2} n,  \log (n !), (\lg n) !,  e^{n}$
  4. $\log ^{2} n, (\lg n) !,  \log (n !),  e^{n}$

Consider functions $f(), g(), \text{and } h()$ which are positive increasing functions.

Also, consider two statements below -

$$\text{S1: If }f(n)=o(g(n)) \text{ then }h(f(n))=o(h(g(n))\text{, here }o\text{ is small-oh} $$

$$\text{S2: If }f(n)=O(g(n)) \text{ then }h(f(n))=O(h(g(n))\text{, here }O\text{ is big-oh}$$

Which of the following is correct ?

  1. $\mathrm{S} 1$ is true but $\mathrm{S} 2$ is false
  2. $\mathrm{S} 1$ is false but $\mathrm{S} 2$ is true
  3. Both statements are true
  4. Both Statements are false

Which of the following(s) is/are true about positive functions
  1. $f(n)=\Omega(g(n)) \Longrightarrow g(n)=O(f(n))$
  2. $f(n)=\omega(g(n)) \Longrightarrow f(n)=\Omega(g(n))$
  3. $f(n)=O(g(n)) \wedge f(n)=\Omega(h(n)) \Longrightarrow g(n)=\Theta(h(n))$
  4. $o(g(n)) \cap \omega(g(n))=\emptyset$

Consider the following $\text{C}$ function:

int  fun1 (int  n)
{ 
    int  i, j, k, p, q =  0;
    for (i = 1; i<n; ++i)
    { 
        p =  0;
        for (j=n; j>1; j=j/2) ++p;
        for (k=1; k<p; k=k*2) ++q;
    }

    return q;
}

Which one of the following most closely approximates the return value of the function $\text{fun1}?$

  1. $n^3$
  2. $n(\log n)^{2}$
  3. $n\log n$
  4. $n \log (\log n)$

Consider a set of functions in $2^{(O(n))}$ which includes all functions of form $2^{(s(n))}$ where $s(n) = O(n)$.

For example :-  $2^{n} = 2^{(O(n))}, 4^{n} = 2^{(O(n))}$ and so on.

Which of the following(s) is/are FALSE?

  1. $f(n)=\left(\frac{n}{2}\right)^{n}$ then $f(n)=2^{\Theta(n \log n)}$
  2. $3^{n}=O\left(2^{n}\right)$
  3. $3^{n}=2^{O(n)}$
  4. $\frac{\ln n}{\sqrt{n}}$ is $O(\sqrt{n})$

Arrange the following functions in their increasing order of growth.

$\left(\begin{array}{c}
\text { If f(n) = O(g(n) and g(n) = O(h((n)) then order is f(n), g(n), h(n).} 
\end{array}\right)$

In all options $\log^{2}n$ means $(\log n)^{2}$

  1. $2^{\log ^{2} n}, \qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n},\qquad 5 \sqrt{n}$
  2. $4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n},\qquad 5 \sqrt{n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n}$
  3. $5 \sqrt{n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n},\qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n}$
  4. $5 \sqrt{n},\qquad 4^{\log n},\qquad 2^{\log ^{2} n},\qquad(\sqrt{2})^{\log n}$

What is the time complexity of following code?

int fun(int n)
{
    int count=0;
    for(int i=n; i>0; i/=2)
        for(int j=0;j<i; j++)

    return count ;

  2. $\Theta(N)$

Consider the case: $f(n)=O(g(n))$. Then, following two statements are claimed to be inferred from the above case.

  • $\text{S1}: 2^{f(n)}=O\left(2^{g(n)}\right)$
  • $\text{S2}: 2^{g(n)}=O\left(2^{f(n)}\right)$

Choose the correct option from the given.

  1. Both correct.
  2. Both incorrect
  3. $\text{S1}$ correct, $\text{S2}$ false
  4. $\text{S2}$ false, $\text{S1}$ correct

  1. $\Omega(\mathrm{n})$

  1. $\Theta\left(\log _{b}(n !)\right)$

What will be the time complexity of following code?

mystery(int N) {
    int i = 1, s = 1;
    while (s <= N) {
        i += 1
        s = s + i;
    }
}

  2. $\Theta(N)$
